chunks: With this chain: from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, that he said: We were told by Ali ibn al-Abbas, that he said: We were told by 'Ubees ibn Hisham, from Abdul-Kareem ibn Amr, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him),
with regards to His saying, Exalted and Glorious is He: «And when I proportioned him and I blew into him from My Spirit» he said: From My Ability.
ai.seo_question: What does 'from My Spirit' mean in Surah Al-Hijr 15:29 according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from Shaykh al-Saduq's *Ma'ani al-Akhbar*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the phrase 'from My Spirit' in the context of creation as referring to God's power (*qudra*) rather than a literal emanation of divine essence. This interpretation aligns with the Shia theological principle of *tawhid* (monotheism), distinguishing between God's attribute of power and His essence to avoid anthropomorphism or substantial division. The explanation underscores that the 'breath' was a divine command manifesting through His creative authority, a view consistent with the broader exegetical tradition regarding the creation of Adam.

en.basel-kadem: 13.	With this chain, from Muhammed bin Isma’il, that he said: We were told by Ali bin Abbas, that he said: We were told by ‘Abees bin Hisham, from Abdul-Kareem bin Amru, from Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him,
with regards to His saying, Exalted and Glorious is He: «And When I proportioned him and I blew into him from My Spirit» [15:29] that he said: (It means) From My Ability.
